steps.tx: **Paraneoplastic syndromes** are remote effects of cancer on the nervous system, occurring without invasion, metastasis, compression or treatment toxicity. They affect only a small fraction of cancer patients, yet the neurologic illness reveals an occult tumour in more than half the cases of cerebellar degeneration. Small cell lung cancer, breast and ovarian adenocarcinoma, thymoma, Hodgkin disease and testicular tumours cause most cases. The antibody often matters more than the tumour size.

steps.tx: **Small cell lung cancer** drives anti-Hu encephalomyelitis, sensory neuronopathy and Lambert Eaton syndrome. Breast and ovarian cancer drive anti-Yo cerebellar degeneration, while breast cancer also yields anti-Ri opsoclonus myoclonus. Testicular tumours pair with anti-Ma brainstem and limbic disease, thymoma with myasthenia and neuromyotonia, and ovarian teratoma with anti-**NMDA receptor** encephalitis. Some patients carry more than one antibody, so panels beat single tests.

steps.tx: **Shared onconeural antigens** explain the attack: the tumour expresses proteins also found in neurons, and the immune response strikes both. Antibodies against surface targets such as NMDA and LGI1 receptors are directly pathogenic and respond to immunotherapy. Antibodies against intracellular targets such as Hu and Yo mark a **T cell** assault that destroys neurons permanently. Tumour immunity may even restrain the cancer, which is why inciting tumours stay tiny and hard to find.

steps.tx: **Lambert Eaton syndrome** is the most common paraneoplastic syndrome: weak proximal legs that briefly strengthen with repeated effort, plus dry mouth and erectile failure. Reflexes return after a few seconds of maximal contraction, and high frequency nerve stimulation markedly increments the response. **Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration** is its mirror: subacute symmetrical ataxia of arms, legs and speech with nystagmus, severe within weeks to months and recognised before the tumour in most cases.

steps.tx: **Limbic encephalitis** brings subacute confusion, agitation, memory loss in a Korsakoff pattern, seizures and hallucinations, with medial temporal inflammation. Anti-NMDA disease strikes young women with a psychiatric prodrome, then dyskinesias, seizures, hypoventilation and sympathetic storms of pulse and pressure. **Opsoclonus myoclonus ataxia** means chaotic dancing eye movements with jerks and gait failure, pointing to neuroblastoma in children and breast or small cell lung cancer in adults.

steps.tx: **Onconeural antibody panels** in serum and CSF open the workup, paired with contrast MRI that shows medial temporal brightness in limbic disease and little early in cerebellar cases. CSF often carries a few dozen lymphocytes with oligoclonal bands. Tumour hunting follows the antibody: chest CT for small cell cancer, mammogram and pelvic imaging for Yo and Ri, testicular ultrasound for Ma, and ovarian imaging for NMDA disease. Whole body **PET** rescues occult cases, and repeat screening continues when the first hunt fails.

steps.tx: **Removing the tumour** is the first treatment: resect the ovarian teratoma, treat the small cell cancer, remove the testicular lesion. Immunotherapy runs in parallel with high dose **methylprednisolone**, intravenous **immunoglobulin** or plasma exchange. Non responders receive **rituximab**, **cyclophosphamide**, **azathioprine** or **mycophenolate**. Seizures need standard anti seizure drugs alongside the immune therapy, and tumour control matters more than antibody titre.

steps.tx: **Surface antibody diseases** such as NMDA and LGI1 encephalitis respond to early rituximab or cyclophosphamide when first line therapy stalls, and most patients recover substantially. Intracellular antibody syndromes with Hu or Yo resist immunotherapy because neurons are already lost, so tumour control dominates. Relapses haunt NMDA disease for years, and antibody positive patients without a found tumour need imaging surveillance every four to six months for up to two years. Checkpoint inhibitor therapy can mimic the same encephalitis picture.

steps.tx: **Hypoventilation** kills in NMDA encephalitis when dysautonomia and depressed drive coincide, and prolonged seizures scar memory circuits. Cerebellar degeneration leaves most survivors with permanent severe ataxia despite tumour cure. Lambert Eaton patients face falls and dysphagia, plus autonomic failure of gut and bladder. Tumour progression, not neurology, decides survival in Hu and Yo disease, while early treated surface antibody patients often return to work with only mild cognitive scars.

steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** Lambert Eaton means small cell lung cancer with facilitating weakness and dry mouth. Anti-Yo means breast or ovarian cancer with subacute pancerebellar ataxia. Anti-Hu means small cell cancer with limbic or sensory neuron disease. Anti-NMDA means young women with ovarian teratoma, psychosis then dyskinesia and hypoventilation. Anti-Ma means testicular tumour, anti-Ri means opsoclonus myoclonus, and tumour removal leads every treatment list.
